results.name: Road Signs Asset Pack | Australian, American
results.description:
Road Sign Asset pack containing 283 unique sign assets depicting road signs in Australia and the United States.

# This model is avaliable for download on [3dmodels.org](https://3dmodels.org/3d-models/australian-and-american-road-signs-asset-pack/) 

**Contains:**
* 104 Warning Sign (Yellow)
* 50 Secondary Warning Signs (Yellow Underneath) - Provide Addition Information
* 11 Pedestrian/Cyclist Warning Sign (Yellow-Green)
* 84 Regulatory signs (White/Black) (Including Speed Limit Signs MPH and KM/H)
* 6 Direction Signs (Green)
* 4 Parking Signs (Blue)
* 7 Hazard Markers (Arrows)
* 10 Various Large Signs
* 7 Various Hazard Signs 

All meshes were modelled by me. Uses Freeway-Gothic and Lane-D fonts
Original Images taken from Wikipedia licensed under public domain. [Australian Road Signs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_signs_in_Australia) [American Road Signs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_signs_in_the_United_States)

results.name: Stern Of SS Rifle
results.description:
This is all that remains of *SS Rifle*, one of the earliest surviving examples of a small pre-fabricated screw steamer in the British Isles. *Rifle* was purchased by the Locheil Estate in the 1860s for use on Loch Arkaig, ferrying goods, passengers and mail between the isolated dwellings around the loch. 

As well as being a practical vessel, *Rifle* was also used for pleasure, often carrying shooting parties. 

The boat was laid-up in the 1930s, and whilst being scrapped, sank and lay buried until removed by the army after becoming a hazard to wartime vessels working from the pier. *Rifle* was blasted away from the pier, losing the bow in the process. 

Despite being submerged for over half a century, it was raised in 1990. Although in a very fragile condition, *Rifle's* propeller is a well-preserved example of an early design. 

The model was created as a part of ‘Scanning The Horizon’ 3D digitisation project.

We would like to thank [RPS Europe](http://www.rpsgroup.com) their help during this project.

results.name: The Poaching Fishermen (by the Seaside Diorama)
results.description:
This is a diorama of a beach in Thailand being used as a base of operations for poaching fishermen. 

The old lighthouse was abandoned when a new, bigger lighthouse was being built closer to the port. Many captains had complained that it was too far away from the new port, and that it was a big safety hazard. The lighthouse was abandoned and stayed that way for 10 years.

During the 1998 Asian financial crisis, many people had to resort to illegal fishing In the area. The old lighthouse seemed like a good place to go fishing, as it was relatively far away from the village but easy to spot from the sea. The fishermen even constructed a small cabin there to hold their equipment.

In 2015, the Thai government got a warning from the European Commision, this warning stated that the government didn't take enough actions against poachers. The poachers near the lighthouse could see a storm coming, and immedeately fled the area as soon as they heard the news. They knew that the lighthouse would soon be searched...

results.name: Super Star (Super Mario Bros)
results.description: Super Stars (also referred to as Starmen, Invincible Stars or simply Stars) are items used in many Mario games, including the Super Mario series and the Mario Kart series. If the player gets a Star, they will become invincible. The user becomes temporarily invulnerable to all damage, being able to defeat anything and carrying up points, except to hazards that would normally be fatal regardless of power-ups (lava, pits, time-over, getting crushed, etc). Most projectiles or enemies that come into contact with the user of the Star while it is activated are destroyed, damaged, or knocked off screen (depending on the type of enemy and what game it is). The Star also increases the speed of the user substantially.
